A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SafeHarbor and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original AgentHarm and AgentSafetyBench evaluations, ablations, efficiency measurements, sensitivity analyses and case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the retrieval, attack-enhancement and frontier-model evaluations moved into Sections 5.5-5.7.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.5 and Algorithm 1 retain the same adversarial generation, hierarchical memory, contrastive safety projector, retrieval and gated LLM judgment procedures.

E1.justification: Both use AgentAlign for memory construction and evaluate on AgentHarm and AgentSafetyBench. The attack scenarios, frontier-model evaluations and appendix case studies are retained; relocation adds no coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Rule Traverse, GuardAgent, RAG, A-Mem, LlamaGuard and AgentAlign, with the same experiment-specific participation. The relocated retrieval and attack-enhancement studies also retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: Dataset sizes, backbone and verifier configurations, evaluation measures, baseline exclusion criteria, ablation settings and threshold sweeps remain unchanged. Removed metric explanations reduce documentation without establishing a changed calculation or protocol.

E4.justification: Table 3 ablations, Figures 3-5 sensitivity and bypass analyses, attack-enhancement validation, memory scaling, judge sensitivity and both case studies retain their evidence. Moving attack-enhancement validation from Appendix D to Section 5.6 adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point-result reporting without repeated-run counts, random-seed specifications, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. Figure 4 shading denotes selected configurations rather than uncertainty.

E6.justification: Matched tables, plots and case studies retain their numerical and qualitative outcomes. Both report GPT-4o benign score 63.6% and harmful refusal 93.2%. The frontier results in v1 Table 8 and v3 Table 7 are identical.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(14), the mathematical reasoning and the notation definitions are unchanged. The notation table is renumbered, with no added or revised theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about precise safety boundaries, reduced over-refusal, efficient deployment and state-of-the-art performance. The abstract's rewritten opening does not alter these claims.

C2.justification: v1 Appendix F broadly emphasizes competitive benign performance across frontier models. v3 Section 5.7 distinguishes small benign-performance changes for GPT-5 and Claude-3.5-Sonnet from Qwen3-32B's larger safety gains, suggesting greater effectiveness for less-aligned models. This revises the interpretation of unchanged results.

D1.justification: v3 removes v1 Table 6's definition of enhancement ASR as successful rewrites among originally failed attacks and Appendix E's definition of Noise Ratio as the proportion of retrieved rules judged purely noisy. Implementation settings, prompt templates, resource information and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Cited-work membership and research positioning remain unchanged. Agrail, A-Mem and WebArena receive publication or year metadata updates, without introducing different prior work.

P1.justification: Three existing appendix studies become Sections 5.5-5.7, and the remaining appendices are reordered and renumbered. Local edits affect the abstract opening, frontier discussion, Impact Statement, author note and bibliography; most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The retrieval, attack-enhancement and frontier-model tables move into the main text, with shortened attack-enhancement and frontier captions. Other tables and appendix figures shift position, while their contents and overall visual design are retained.

improvement.justification: Moving existing analyses into Sections 5.5-5.7 improves their visibility, and the frontier discussion becomes more specific. However, deleting the conditional ASR definition and the Noise Ratio explanation makes unchanged results less precisely interpretable and reproducible. These documentation losses outweigh the modest presentation gains.
